chapter_mission: Bring Ben home, have him tell Luke the truth in person, and close the book on shared honesty rather than solitary burden.
chapter_turn: The mission briefing room becomes the room where Ben stops withholding. The last movement is small and human: tell the truth, let Luke answer it, walk the corridor again changed.

scene_plan.purpose: Ben deletes every version of the report because this truth has to be spoken in person. The new chord under his perception should follow him all the way home.
Ben tells Luke the whole story. Luke listens, names the silence between them once, and chooses the truth with him.
Walk Ben back through the corridor from Chapter 1 and let the change live in perception, pace, and body rather than in summary.

relationship_turns.from: active deception (Ch15); specific unmade call (Ch 13, Ch 14)
relationship_turns.to: father-son candor — the Ch1 briefing room is the Ch28 reckoning room. Luke listens without invoking Grand Master rank; Ben speaks without pretending he did this alone. The institutional distance the novel opened with is the private alliance it closes with. Per PP26 payoff, Luke's 'And you didn't call me' names the unmade Ch 13 call without requiring Ben to defend it. Ben's Ch1 relationship turn reversed and resolved

institutional honesty committed to — Luke's 'We'll tell the Council. All of it' is the Order's decision to stop carrying the thousand-year lie. Per D5, merged SP3 (institutional honesty / truth-telling) resolves not as Ben's confession but as a shared choice between father and son

at peace with the name — the corridor walk is the Ch1 walk inverted. Ben has not earned his name by being more or less than his family. He has redefined the word by being himself inside a chord he did not write alone. A note is enough

exit_vector: 'A note in a chord. Enough.' The book ends on Ben's footsteps continuing down a corridor he has walked since he was a child. The wrongness is silent. The resonance hums. The renewal tether sits in the edge of perception. The Order will know. The work continues.
notes: Restraint matters here. Delete the drafts, tell the story, let Luke's question name the wound between them, and stop. The chapter should close on geography, body, and perception rather than retrospective explanation. Luke is sad, not angry. Ben is steadier, not sainted. The corridor walk should feel lived-in and ordinary enough that the chord under it matters.
